newsitem.title: USA: U.S. first-time jobless claims lowest in 23 years.
newsitem.headline: U.S. first-time jobless claims lowest in 23 years.

text.p: The number of Americans making first-time claims for jobless benefits fell last week to the lowest level in more than 23 years, the government reported on Thursday.
Weekly jobless claims fell to 277,000 in the week ended July 26 from 299,000 the week before. That undershot Wall Street economists' consensus forecast of 306,000.
The four-week moving average, which helps smooth out any big week-to-week swings in the data, slipped to 325,750 from 340,750 the week before.
The number of Americans filing claims to continue their benefits rose slightly, to 2,335,000 in the week ended July 19, the latest period for which those data were available.
Labour said 48 states and territories recorded declines in initial claims on an unadjusted basis in the week ended July 19, while five reported an increase.
Twenty-two states and Puerto Rico saw initial claims dip by more than 1,000, unadjusted, during the July 19 week.
States reporting the greatest declines were Michigan, with 24,694 fewer, Indiana, down 6,004, Pennsylvania, off 5,587, and North Carolina, with 5,138 fewer claims.
Michigan cited fewer layoffs in the automobile industry. Indiana reported fewer layoffs related to the apparel and transportation equipment industries.
Pennsylvania also saw fewer transportation-related layoffs, but in addition had fewer layoffs in the rubber/plastics, primary metals and fabricated metals industries.
North Carolina said fewer layoffs among textile and furniture workers contributed to its decline in initial claims.

Two states, Missouri and Ohio, recorded increases of more than 1,000 claims on an unadjusted basis. An increase in transportation-related layoffs pushed the claims figure higher in Missouri, while layoffs in various industries scattered throughout the state added to claims in Ohio, the department said.
